target.title: fix(telegram): long-running sends leak connections after cache evictions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running Telegram senders could keep abandoned HTTP transports alive when the Telegram client options cache evicted old account/network entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cache entry now retains the transport created for its client fetch so eviction can release the old dispatcher lifecycle instead of only deleting the client options object. Evicted entries are retired immediately, but their transport is closed only after active send-level leases finish, so cache pressure does not abort an in-flight Telegram send.

## User Impact

Operators running Telegram channels with many account or network option combinations should see stale Telegram transports released after cache eviction instead of accumulating idle connections over time, without changing existing Telegram send behavior for active requests.

## Evidence

- Live/near-real proof passed with a local Telegram Bot API substitute and the real `sendMessageTelegram` entry point. The run sent through 65 distinct production-mode account cache entries, observed 65 HTTP `POST /bot.../sendMessage` requests, and observed 6 undici dispatcher `destroy()` calls after cache eviction.
- Focused Telegram proxy regression passed: 1 file passed, 7 tests passed. The regressions drive 65 production-mode cache entries, verify the evicted transport `close()` is called, and verify eviction defers `close()` until the active send finishes.
- Extensions type checking passed with `pnpm tsgo:test:extensions`.
- `OPENCLAW_DEV_AUTO_PAIR=false start_openclaw_dev_gateway.sh` — isolated OpenClaw dev gateway reached ready; the startup log recorded `http server listening` and `ready`.

Before the fix, the eviction regression failed with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times` for the evicted transport close spy. The lease regression covers the active-send case that would be unsafe if eviction closed the transport immediately.
